From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Structured Output reliability & SDK integration (Fjord)

Thanks again for the sync earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration, auth, and structured-output reliability patterns.

Recap (high level)
- Fjord goal: embed a structured Q&A assistant that returns constrained JSON payloads (order, amount, line_items) and supports reranking/embeddings for document retrieval.
- Primary constraints: deterministic JSON schema validation, auditability, and graceful retries when constrained decoding fails.
- Integration preference: server-side SDK with key-based service account, routed to Redwood Dedicated initially, fallback to hosted for burst.

Action items / next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll share a recommended JSON schema and decoding strategy (attached: structured-output-schema.json). Suggest binding schema validation into the server-side call flow with a post-response validation step + retry-with-backoff that tightens decoding constraints on retry.
2) SDK quickstart + auth: attach redwood-sdk-quickstart.md showing service-account key provisioning, example auth headers, and sample streaming callback wiring for structured outputs.
3) Embeddings/reranker: Mateo will draft a suggested retrieval pipeline that uses embeddings for candidate generation and a lightweight reranker using a small instruction-tuned model (we discussed cost/latency tradeoffs).
4) POC timeline & scope: propose a 2-week POC (week 1: SDK + schema validation + sample doc retriever; week 2: reranker + reliability tests + failure-mode drill). We can run the POC on Redwood Dedicated dev pool.

Reliability patterns we recommend (summary)
- Constrained decoding: use schema-guided token constraints + sampling temperature 0.0 for determinism on the first attempt.
- Validation: immediate JSON schema validation (strict) with clear error codes; if validation fails, automatically retry with a stronger constraint profile (e.g., token whitelist + forced keys) up to N=2 retries. Capture both raw and validated payloads in audit logs.
- Latency vs correctness: if retries push past your latency SLO, surface a partial fallback payload with a validation failure flag and provide the last-known-good cached response.

Attachments: structured-output-schema.json (JSON schema), redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (setup + auth samples), poC-mvp-plan.pdf (timeline + success criteria).

Questions for you
- Are there any compliance constraints around storing raw LLM responses temporarily for debugging? (we can subset logs or use ephemeral storage).
- Do you have an internal SLA/latency budget for the endpoint? Helps us size retry budgets.

Suggested next meeting: 30-min technical kickoff (engineers only) — propose Wed 2026-08-12 10:00 PDT.

Happy to adapt — ping if you want us to convert the schema to your internal types first.

—
Marissa Cole

3) SDKs: do you have sample validators in Java (we run a JVM-heavy stack) or should we adapt the Node example?

Samir — great questions, answers inline below + next steps.

1) Compliance/logging: yes. Our audit log pipeline supports encryption at rest using customer-managed keys (KMS) and per-tenant retention policies. We can configure the debug-store to expire raw LLM responses after 30 days for this POC. I’ve noted this as a requirement in the POC plan.

2) Failure modes / partial payloads: recommended approach:
   - Primary response: validated JSON matching the schema.
   - If validation fails after retries: return an object with keys "status":"partial", "errors":[...validation messages...], "fallback":{...cached_or_minimal_fields...}. Example payload attached in the schema file comments. Downstream services can key on status=="partial" and route to a lightweight compensating flow.

3) SDK validators: we have community-contrib Java validators in our examples repo (link below). For the POC we can ship a small Java helper that wraps the validation + retry loop; alternatively, your engineers can call the Node helper over an internal RPC if you prefer not to bring Java in initially.

4) Calendar invite & agenda: sent — please confirm attendees. Agenda: 1) quick architecture overview (10m), 2) SDK auth + sample call (10m), 3) validation/retry patterns + success criteria (10m).

POC start / Success criteria
- Target start: Mon 2026-08-17 (we’ll provision a Dedicated dev pool).
- Success criteria (end of week 2): end-to-end pipeline that returns validated payloads >= 95% of test cases for our canned prompt set; autoscaling verified under 50 concurrent requests; and audit logs streaming to your secure bucket.

Attachments & links: structured-output-schema.json, SDK examples on GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/structured-output-validation, POC plan here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e/structured-output-spec

If that all looks good I’ll loop in infra and schedule a short kickoff.
